memory_update.text: PAR is the strongest underfollowed public mapping for restaurant first-party data rails because it combines POS, loyalty, ordering, and payments exposure at small-cap scale.
Shift4 should remain in the Layer 1 universe as a payments-labeled company with hidden restaurant POS, ordering, loyalty, and analytics exposure through SkyTab.

Toast and DoorDash are high-attention reference anchors: Toast benchmarks integrated restaurant operating-system economics, while DoorDash benchmarks aggregator leverage and marketplace demand access.

Olo was likely the cleanest pure-play public candidate for this node, but it was acquired by Thoma Bravo in September 2025 and should be tracked only as a private-market comp, not as a US-listed candidate.

node: Delivery channels, first-party ordering, loyalty data, and aggregator partnerships
summary: Layer 1B expands the public-company universe around restaurant digital-ordering/data rails. The chokepoint is not simply delivery capacity; it is control of customer identity, order origination, loyalty, payments, POS integration, and aggregator routing. Olo would have been the cleanest pure-play public comp, but it was taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2025, leaving PAR Technology, Shift4, Toast, and DoorDash as the most relevant US-listed public mappings for this pass. The underfollowed lane is strongest in PAR and Shift4 because they sit inside restaurant operating systems rather than consumer-facing delivery apps.
